examples: There is a computer on the desk.
I read a book on the bed.
I put the bag on the chair.
nuance: 위 means the top side or above something and joins a noun like 책상 위 to show position.
mistakes: Saying 위에서 있어요 instead of 위에 있어요 for existence.

examples: There is a bag under the chair.
I eat lunch under the tree.
I put the book under the bed.
nuance: 아래 means the area below or under something and pairs with a noun like 책상 아래 for position.
mistakes: Using 밑 and 아래 interchangeably without noticing 밑 is more casual.

usage: it is in front of the door
I meet in front of the station
examples: There is a shop in front of the school.
I wait for my friend in front of the cafe.
I park the car in front of the house.
nuance: 앞 means the front side or the area ahead and joins a noun like 집 앞 to mark position.
mistakes: Saying 앞에서 있어요 instead of 앞에 있어요 for existence.

examples: There is a parking lot behind the building.
The puppy sleeps behind the house.
I put the bicycle behind the shop.
nuance: 뒤 means the back side or the area behind and joins a noun like 집 뒤 to show position.
mistakes: Confusing 뒤 (behind) with 후 (after) since 후 marks time.

usage: it is next to the bank
I wait next to the station
examples: There is a desk next to the window.
I take the bus next to the cafe.
I put the bag next to the bed.
nuance: 옆 means the side or the spot right next to something and joins a noun like 창문 옆.
mistakes: Saying 옆에서 있어요 instead of 옆에 있어요 for existence.

examples: There is a key inside the bag.
I listen to music inside the room.
I put the umbrella inside the bag.
nuance: 안 means the inside or interior of a space and joins a noun like 가방 안 to mark position.
mistakes: Using 가방에 instead of 가방 안에 when you mean inside it.

examples: There is a person outside the door.
I meet my friend outside the house.
I leave the shoes outside the door.
nuance: 밖 means the outside or exterior of a place and joins a noun like 집 밖 to show position.
mistakes: Saying 밖에서 있어요 instead of 밖에 있어요 for existence.

examples: There is a shop between the bank and the cafe.
I take a photo between the two trees.
I put the chair between the desks.
nuance: 사이 means the space between two things and often uses 와 or 과 to link both sides.
mistakes: Forgetting 과 or 와 when naming both things on each side.

usage: to the left of the door
it is to the left of the bank
I meet on the left of the station
examples: There is a mirror to the left of the door.
I take the bus on the left of the shop.
I put the bag on the left of the bed.
nuance: 왼쪽 means the left side or left direction and joins a noun like 문 왼쪽 to mark position.
mistakes: Mixing up 왼쪽 (left) with 오른쪽 (right) when giving directions.

usage: to the right of the door
it is to the right of the cafe
I wait on the right of the station
examples: There is a bank to the right of the cafe.
I meet my friend on the right of the building.
I put the chair on the right of the desk.
nuance: 오른쪽 means the right side or right direction and joins a noun like 문 오른쪽 to show position.
mistakes: Mixing up 오른쪽 (right) with 왼쪽 (left) when giving directions.

examples: There is a park near my house.
I meet my friend near the station.
There are many cafes near the office.
nuance: 근처 means the nearby area or vicinity around a place and joins a noun like 집 근처.
mistakes: Saying 근처에서 있어요 instead of 근처에 있어요 for existence.

usage: in the middle of the room
it is in the middle of the room
I rest in the middle of the park
examples: There is a table in the middle of the room.
Children play in the middle of the park.
I put the chair in the middle of the room.
nuance: 가운데 means the middle or center point of a space and joins a noun like 방 가운데.
mistakes: Using 가운데 for between two items, where 사이 fits better.
